tasks.title: free_model_probe.py — free-window health gate CLI
tasks.spec:
Write a standalone Python 3 CLI script (STDLIB ONLY, no third-party imports) named free_model_probe.py that checks whether a model on the Nous inference API is currently free.

Behavior:
- Usage: free_model_probe.py <model_id> [--base-url URL] [--timeout SECONDS]
- Reads the bearer token from the JSON file /opt/data/shared/nous_auth.json, key "access_token".
- GET {base_url}/v1/models (default base_url https://inference-api.nousresearch.com) with an Authorization: Bearer header AND a User-Agent header (the server returns 403 without a User-Agent).
- Find the entry whose id equals the model_id. If absent, print one JSON object {"model": model_id, "present": false, "free": false} and exit 2.
- free means pricing.prompt == 0 AND pricing.completion == 0 (numbers may be int or float or string; coerce with float()).
- Canary check: POST {base_url}/v1/chat/completions with {"model": model_id, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK"}], "max_tokens": 5}; canary_ok = HTTP 200.
- Print ONE JSON object to stdout with keys: model, present, free, price_in_per_token, price_out_per_token, canary_ok, checked_at (ISO 8601 UTC string).
- Exit code 0 if present AND free AND canary_ok; exit 1 otherwise. On any internal error print {"error": "..."} and exit 1 — never raise a traceback. HTTP timeouts must be handled.

tasks.title: board_report.py — one-glance worker board status
tasks.spec:
Write a standalone Python 3 CLI script (STDLIB ONLY) named board_report.py that prints a compact status report of the worker board.

Behavior:
- Usage: board_report.py [board_path]  (default /opt/data/missingno-worker/board.json)
- The board JSON has shape {"window": {"status": str, ...}, "tasks": [{"id": str, "title": str, "status": str, "attempts": int, "updated_at": str-or-null}, ...]}.
- Print first line exactly: BOARD: <pending> pending, <done> done, <failed> failed | window: <window.status>
- Then one line per task in file order: <id> | <status> | attempts=<attempts> | <title>
- pending counts tasks with status pending or in_progress.
- Exit 0 on success. If the file is missing or invalid JSON, print one error line to stderr and exit 1. Never raise a traceback.

tasks.title: bench_harness.py — mini coding-benchmark runner with --self-test
tasks.verify_cmd: /opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python tasks_out/bench_harness.py --model stealth/missingno --self-test | /opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d.get('pass_rate')==1.0, d; assert d['results'][0]['passed'] is True; print('VERIFY-OK')"
tasks.spec:
Write a standalone Python 3 CLI script (STDLIB ONLY) named bench_harness.py that runs a model on small coding prompts and grades the results.

Behavior:
- Usage: bench_harness.py --model <model_id> [--prompts FILE] [--self-test]
- Bearer token from JSON file /opt/data/shared/nous_auth.json key "access_token"; API base https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1/chat/completions; always send a User-Agent header.
- Prompts file (default /opt/data/missingno-worker/bench_prompts.json) is a JSON list of {"id": str, "prompt": str, "checks": [{"expr": str}]}. Each prompt asks the model for a small pure Python function; "expr" is a Python expression evaluated with the function's return value bound to the variable "result".
- For each prompt: call the model (max_tokens 1000), extract the last ```python fenced code block (or the whole response if no fence), exec it in a fresh namespace, then call the function under test with the example arguments given in the prompt text, bind the return value to "result", and evaluate each check expr with eval(expr, {"result": result}). A prompt passes if all its checks evaluate truthy and nothing raised.
- If the prompts file does not exist, CREATE it with 3 prompts: add(a, b) returns the sum (check: result == 7 for add(3, 4)); is_palindrome(s) True for 'racecar' (check: result is True); count_vowels(s) counts vowels case-insensitively (check: result == 3 for 'Beautiful'). Each prompt must state the exact function signature and the example call to use.
- --self-test: ignore the prompts file and use one canned prompt: implement add(a, b) returning the sum, call add(3, 4), check result == 7.
- Print ONE JSON object to stdout: {"model": model_id, "results": [{"id": ..., "passed": true/false}], "pass_rate": <float>}. Exit 0 if the harness ran (even with failures), exit 1 only on internal error (bad token, unreadable file, etc.) — never a traceback. Wrap each model call in 3 retries with short sleeps on 429/timeout.

tasks.spec:
Write a standalone Python 3 module (STDLIB ONLY) yt_transcript_fallback.py with:
(1) parse_timedtext(xml_text) -> list of {'start': float, 'dur': float, 'text': str} parsed from YouTube timedtext XML (<text start="1.2" dur="0.5">escaped text</text> entries; use xml.etree, unescape HTML entities).
(2) parse_player_response(html) -> dict: extract the JSON assigned to 'ytInitialPlayerResponse' in a page's inline script (find the substring, json.loads the balanced-brace object) and return it; return {} if not found.
(3) caption_track_urls(player_response) -> list of caption track 'baseUrl' strings from player_response['captions']['playerCaptionsTracklistRenderer']['captionTracks']; return [] on any missing key.
(4) if __name__ == '__main__': accept a --selftest flag that runs the three functions on small embedded samples and prints PASS; accept a --video-id ID flag that (best-effort, network) tries https://www.youtube.com/api/timedtext?v=ID&lang=en and prints the parsed caption count.
All functions must be importable; never raise tracebacks on bad input (return [] or {}).

tasks.spec:
Write a standalone Python 3 server worker_office_server.py (STDLIB ONLY, use http.server) that serves the live worker office data.

Behavior:
- CLI: worker_office_server.py [--port N] [--board PATH] [--log PATH]; defaults port 8798, board /opt/data/missingno-worker/board.json, log /opt/data/missingno-worker/logs/tick.log.
- GET /api/board -> JSON: {"window": <window object from board.json>, "tasks": <tasks list from board.json>, "recent_ticks": [last 10 non-empty lines of the tick log]}. Read board.json FRESH on every request (no caching). If the board file is unreadable, return {"error": "board unreadable"} with HTTP 500.
- GET / -> serves the file worker_office.html from the same directory as the script (Content-Type text/html); if missing, serve a minimal HTML page containing the text 'worker_office.html not built yet' with HTTP 200.
- Bind 127.0.0.1 ONLY (loopback). ThreadingHTTPServer. Clean shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM. No tracebacks in normal operation. Print one startup line to stdout: 'worker office serving on 127.0.0.1:<port>'.

tasks.title: P4: worker_office.js — 2.5D pixel office canvas client
tasks.verify_cmd: cd /opt/data/missingno-worker && node --check tasks_out/worker_office.js && node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const s=fs.readFileSync('tasks_out/worker_office.js','utf8'); ['init(','fetch(','requestAnimationFrame','getContext'].every(k=>s.includes(k)) || process.exit(1); console.log('MARKERS-OK')" && echo VERIFY-OK
tasks.spec:
Write a single JavaScript file worker_office.js (plain ES2020, no imports, no external libraries) that renders a 2.5D pixel-art office on an HTML canvas.

Requirements:
- A global function init(canvas, apiBase) that starts everything; use it for the window.onload handler. Poll apiBase + '/api/board' every 5 seconds with fetch() and update the scene.
- Canvas rendering with getContext('2d') and requestAnimationFrame for a ~30fps game loop.
- Draw a simple isometric/pixel office floor: a tiled floor grid (drawn as filled polygons or rects), at least 4 desks (rects with darker outline), and one wall along the back.
- Characters (8-16px pixel figures drawn with fillRect blocks, not images): (1) THE WORKER — a small character that walks between desks; its state comes from the board data: a pending task = worker walks to that desk and a 'building' bubble; in_progress = animated typing at the desk; done = green flash + walk to next; failed = red bubble. (2) Tasks render as small glowing documents on desks: grey=pending, blue=in_progress, green=done, red=failed.
- A status bar at the top of the canvas (fillText): window status (OPEN in green / CLOSED in red) and counts of pending/done/failed.
- Handle fetch errors gracefully: if the API is unreachable show 'OFFLINE' in the status bar, keep animating, never throw.
- Deterministic pseudo-random walk offsets are fine; no network calls other than the poll. No console spam.
- The file must be syntactically valid standalone (it will be checked with node --check).

tasks.spec:
Write a single HTML file worker_office.html (no external assets, no CDN, no images) that hosts the worker office.

Requirements:
- DOCTYPE html, title 'Worker Office', dark background (#1a1a2e or similar), centered full-viewport layout.
- One <canvas id="office-canvas"> that scales responsively (width 960 height 600 attributes, CSS max-width 100%).
- Loads the client with <script src="worker_office.js"></script> and calls init(document.getElementById('office-canvas'), '/api/board') on load (a tiny inline script is fine — keep it under 5 lines, no backticks in it).
- A small fixed footer line: 'missingno worker office — loopback only'.
- Nothing else: no network calls, no fonts fetched, no inline SVG libraries.
